A great castle perched atop a vast floating chunk of mountain, its cracked underside trailing roots and broken earth, drifting alone through open sky with banks of cloud scrolling far below its shadow.
A chain of linked floating sky-isles, each crowned with white towers and lit gardens, joined by long arching bridges of pale stone, strung in a grand arc across the open heavens.
An airborne fortress of dark spires bristling from a jagged floating crag, iron banners streaming in the high wind, the sheer void dropping away in every direction beneath its scarred foundations.
A castle built atop an upside-down mountain, its peak plunging downward into open air, its flat shattered base bearing towers and walls high above the clouds, impossibly inverted against the sky.
A palace seated on a broad disc of floating rock, long tangled roots spilling from its rim and trailing into empty air, the whole structure gliding slow and silent through golden afternoon light.
An archipelago of tiny floating islets scattered across a wide stretch of sky, each one just large enough for a tower or a keep, connected by rope bridges swaying in the open wind.

A citadel built deep inside a hollow floating crag, its towers visible through great broken windows in the rock face, torchlight flickering from within, the entire crag drifting through a sea of cloud.

A ring-shaped sky-fortress, its circular wall enclosing a vast open courtyard of gardens and spires, the whole structure rotating slowly in the high atmosphere, cloud streaming through its central void.
A temple rising from a single soaring needle of rock hanging in open sky, its colonnaded halls carved directly from the spire, accessible only by air, unreachable from any ground below.

A castle perpetually wrapped in its own private storm, dark clouds churning around its towers, lightning tracing its battlements, hail and thunder constant, the whole turbulent mass drifting through otherwise clear skies.
A golden sky-palace resting on a sunlit cloud-isle of impossible density, its domed rooftops blazing in full sun above a floor of white cloud, the world below entirely hidden from its inhabitants.
A vast stepped citadel carved from a single floating mesa, each tier bearing colonnades and hanging gardens, the flat underside of the mesa smooth as glass, suspended over an ocean of open air.

A cathedral-castle of white stone thrust from a narrow floating ridge, flying buttresses arcing out over sheer drops, its tallest spire vanishing into a ceiling of low cloud, the ridge drifting eastward in silence.

A fortress city sprawled across three massive floating boulders chained together, streets and towers bridging the gaps, the chains groaning in the wind, all three rocks swaying in loose formation through the sky.

A sky-palace of crystal domes and glass towers perched on a luminous floating island, the island itself glowing faintly from within, casting pale light downward through the cloud layer far beneath it.
A tiered castle of black basalt standing on a floating volcanic plug, old lava columns hanging from its underside, thin smoke curling upward from cracks in the rock, adrift in cold high-altitude air.
A grand keep surrounded by an entire floating forest, ancient trees growing to the very edge of the rock, their roots visible at the crumbling rim, the whole wooded island drifting through open sky.

A sky-citadel built across a cluster of floating stone arches, its halls suspended between pillars of rock that connect nothing below, towers rising from the keystones of arches hanging over infinite open air.

A palace of bone-white towers encircling a central spire so tall it pierces the cloud above, the whole complex seated on a floating oval of pale stone, drifting through the upper atmosphere in silence.

A military sky-fortress shaped like a great wedge of rock, its forward face sheer and featureless, its flat top crowded with towers and siege engines, driving through the sky like a stone ship under sail.

A floating isle of red sandstone honeycombed with carved chambers, its exterior face covered in windows and balconies, towers erupting from its top, the whole eroded mass hanging in warm orange evening light.
A castle growing from a floating glacier, its towers of ice rising translucent and blue above the frozen mass, meltwater streaming from its edges in long silver threads falling into the sky below.

A sky-stronghold wrapped around a floating sphere of ancient rock, buildings covering every surface including the underside, so that no matter the angle some tower points outward into open air above the clouds.

A grand floating pavilion-palace of lacquered red and gold, seated on a cloud of impossible solidity, flanked by hanging gardens trailing vines into open air, visible for a hundred miles in clear morning sky.

A ruined sky-castle, half its mountain already fallen away, remaining towers leaning over open void, broken bridges hanging from single anchor points, the fractured rock drifting slowly through evening cloud, magnificent and crumbling.
